newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon growth slows to four pct in 1996 - B.Audi.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon growth slows to four pct in 1996 - B.Audi.

text.p: Lebanon's economic growth slowed to an estimated four percent in 1996 from seven percent in 1995, Banque Audi said.
"The Lebanese economy showed signs of fatigue in 1996," the bank said in its economic report for the fourth quarter of 1996.
"GNP, driven more by consumption than by investment, grew according to our estimates by four percent in real terms compared with 1995 when it grew by seven percent," it said.
It attributed the slowdown to the following factors:
- Israel's 17-day Grapes of Wrath blitz in April 1996 which caused damage estimated at $400-$500 million "which represents an approximate reduction of one percent in real growth of GDP."

- The crowding-out effects of the authorities' expensive currency policy which had the effect of giving the state the benefit of 48.7 percent of total bank loans to economic sectors "thus depriving the private sector of substantial resources," and

- The effects of the policy of austerity on public investment, which fell by 7.5 percent in real terms, influenced private investment which generated less added value, thus having a negative effect on growth.
